name: How much contingency should a luxury custom home budget include?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should be included in a high-end home construction budget in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should be included in a high-end home construction budget in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Luxury custom homes should not be budgeted as if every detail is known on day one. A contingency is used for unforeseen conditions, permit-related scope changes, and owner-driven adjustments. For complex Los Angeles projects, the contingency should be larger when the lot is sloped, the home is highly customized, or the design is still evolving. It should be separate from finish allowances, which cover items like tile, fixtures, appliances, and cabinetry. Homeowners should ask the builder exactly what the contingency can and cannot be used for, who approves its use, and how spending is reported. A well-managed contingency does not mean the project is poorly planned; it is a normal safeguard for premium construction where details are refined over time. The key is to define it early and keep it transparent throughout the build.
acceptedAnswer.description: A luxury home budget should usually include a contingency because high-end projects face design changes, site surprises, and pricing shifts. Many owners plan for a project contingency plus separate allowances for finishes and upgrades. The more complex the site or architecture, the larger the contingency should be.
